newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan grain/oilseeds buying slow ahead of holiday.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan grain/oilseeds buying slow ahead of holiday.

text.p: Taiwanese buying of grains and oilseeds is expected to be sluggish next week ahead of the Chinese Lunar New Year holiday which falls between February 6 to February 10 this year, traders said on Friday.

An expected highlight of limited forthcoming business is Hui Shung Group's expected retender on Tuesday or Wednesday for a combined shipment of 38,000 tonnes of soybeans and 16,000 tonnes of corn, traders said.
Local buyers said they are interested in Argentine corn and expect to see world prices fall in late February as the market comes under increasing pressure from Argentine supply.
Taiwan buyers would consider buying Argentine corn if the prices were about US$10 a tonne lower than U.S. corn, they said.
"There isn't much support for corn futures in the near term and pressure from the Argentine harvest will increase in February," one trader said.
The Taiwan Flour Mills Association is not expected to return to the international wheat market next week, association official Lu Wei-chih told Reuters.

Dry bulk freight rates between the Pacific Northwest and Taiwan were quoted at about US$14.00 a tonne and from the Gulf of Mexico at between $22.00 and $22.50 a tonne, both for Panamax-sized March shipments.
